This is probably obvious to a lot of people here, but maybe some of you don't know. Chrome has similar features.

Style Editor

Shift+F7 show you the Style Editor. You can detach it to another window for a better navigation.

You can see what's in the CSS of the page you're browsing, or even create a new style sheet with New button and put your code there. It will reflect to the page immediatelly.

Inspector

To discover the names of ids and classes, you can press Shift+Ctrl+C, and pass the mouse over things to see how they're called in the HTML code.

So, for example, open some subverse, Shift+Ctrl+C, mouse over sidebar, it's called div.side. DIV is HTML, .side is a CSS class. Shift+F7, create a new stylesheet (or use the one you already created), type 

.side {
/*put your magic here*/
}

Apparently, some newlines are needed after the last }
